note: Steps of the plan, by milestone. gather.py keeps a 'done' or 'done-emu' step only while every pull request it names is merged with CI passing on the commit that brought it into main; otherwise it drops the step to 'review' or 'progress' and says why. The tag of each step (merged, in review, in progress or planned) comes from gh. 'done-emu' means checked on the host, in WASM under Node and Bun, or in headless DOSBox; nothing has run on real hardware. Milestones 0 to 6 are the working plan, with Milestone 1.5 (id m1_5) between Milestones 1 and 2, Milestone 3.5 (id m3_5) after Milestone 3 and Milestone 6 (Shell) last; Milestones 3.5 and 6 are placeholders with no start date; the order of Milestones 2 to 5 follows the restart plan in docs/POC-1-FINDINGS.md.

milestones.label: M1 · The first playable slice
milestones.next: The documentation phase: the archive refresh for the slice and the release changelog. The rest of the milestone is merged.

milestones.label: M1.5 · Machine, settings and DOS audio
milestones.next: The Options screen with the settings it changes, the frame-rate policy measured, a live HUD, the HUD extras (ammo in red at zero, a key chip, a toast line and a level-name banner) and the Motion setting on DOS. The probes, the check screen, the sound settings, the help screen and DOS audio are built; the milestone's own test, the cluck audible on DOS, has not been done because nobody has listened.

milestones.label: M2 · Content pipeline
milestones.next: The real work has not started. The sprite grids and the generated sprite data exist; the first fizz-bake step is a Level Studio script baked into a Fizz Asset Pack (`.FAP`), with a per-target profile. The Fizz 1 survey adds the enemy roster with animation states, animated tiles, backdrop art for parallax and the export of the stars sprite. New Episode 2 design, not ports: idle blinks and orbiting dizzy stars, with run dust and a landing squash proposed.

milestones.label: M3 · Scene intent and camera
milestones.next: The real work has not started. A shared pixel rule, a stateless look offset and the shared drawing exist; fizz-engine with scene intent is next, then the camera with Fizz 1's pixel-locking, shown on Web and DOS. The Fizz 1 survey adds Fizz 1's camera constants and Tower mode, shake for the remaining events, drawing between ticks on Web, point lights with a DOS 16-colour shade pass, night profiles, parallax layers and a general effects list.

milestones.label: M3.5 · Mechanics roster
milestones.next: Placeholder with no start date. Nothing is started. Wall-kick comes first, because the lighthouse level is vertical; score, snacks and lives wait for an Episode 2 decision.

milestones.label: M4 · Audio
milestones.next: Builds on M1.5's detection and routing. The effects pipeline exists (the cluck source, the OPL2 and speaker downmixes, fizz-sfx and Web playback); the work left is Fizz 1's other sound effects for the slice, with their captions (the head-bump clunk, the shot's fzzt, the pogo boing, the key, the door, stun and hurt), and the music: lowering the IMF lab's composition to OPL2 and OPL3 arrangements for DOS and playing it on Web. The full caption table (including whoa!, ta-da!, click - no fizz, bonk, fizzled and crunch) and positional pan and gain on Web join the work.

milestones.label: M5 · CI gates and the 486 budget
milestones.next: Keeps the CI cycle gate and the size budgets. /BENCH, its calibration line and the tracked size exist; the budgets are measured against a 486DX model and gated in CI.

milestones.label: M6 · Shell
milestones.next: Placeholder with no start date. Nothing is started: title, pause, options, four save slots, result cards and the opening cinematic; haptics and a debug level select come later.

nodes.label: Mode 13h presenter

nodes.label: FIZZ2.EXE

nodes.label: View helpers

nodes.evidence: cargo test -p fizz-view; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Web view

nodes.label: Slice drawing on both presenters
nodes.what: The slice drawn by the same routine on DOS (mode 13h, retrace wait) and the Web canvas, with Fizz 1's run cycle and the two-legged chicken.

nodes.label: Retire fizz-hello
nodes.what: The throwaway rules are deleted and the parity gate compares the slice instead.

nodes.label: The cluck as an event
nodes.what: The chicken's random cluck as a deterministic named event in the rules.

nodes.label: Cluck source with four variants
nodes.what: The cluck sound source, its OPL2 and speaker downmixes, fizz-sfx, and a repeated fourth variant.

nodes.label: Web audio with Undertone
nodes.what: The cluck played on the Web with Undertone, with a mute (M), silence on a hidden tab and at most four clucks at once. A stand-in AudioContext records what is scheduled; nobody has listened.

nodes.label: /BENCH and the drawing speed-up
nodes.what: The DOS /BENCH mode that times the step, the drawing and the copy; a faster slice drawing measured with it; and the corrected cycle setting. DOSBox at a fixed 26,800 cycles a millisecond; a 486 has not been measured.

nodes.label: The chicken's beak and captions
nodes.what: The chicken opens its beak and a caption floats when it clucks, with /NOCAPTIONS and /CAPTIONS on DOS and a Captions button and V on the Web.

nodes.label: Look and aim
nodes.what: Look up, look down and aim up and down, proven against Fizz 1 by the look and aim traces.

nodes.label: Documentation phase
nodes.what: The player's manual, the reference documents and the work log are merged; a refresh of this archive for the slice is in review.

nodes.label: Stun stars
nodes.what: Fizz 1's two-frame 16x8 stars sprite, twinkling at 6 Hz and drawn 0.3 tile above a stunned enemy, with Fizz 2's alert frame and last-second flash. View only: the rules do not change. Grabbed from DOSBox and headless Chromium; not looked at on real hardware.
nodes.evidence: fizz-slice-view tests (pinned frame at tick 700); media/dos-stars.png

nodes.label: Shot-end puff
nodes.what: A view-only event when a shot ends, drawn as Fizz 1's four-frame puff. The event added three lines to the golden transcript.
nodes.evidence: slice-replay.txt EVENT shotend lines; fizz-slice-view tests

nodes.label: Death shake
nodes.what: A screen shake of at most a pixel for 18 ticks, derived from Ben's dead state, so the rules gain no new state. The Web Motion button turns it off; DOS always shakes. No still shows it, and it has not been looked at on DOS.

nodes.label: Web fill-page
nodes.what: The Web canvas fills the window and follows its shape: 13 tiles tall, 96 to 1,280 pixels wide, with the controls in an overlay panel (H).

nodes.label: Web caption overlay
nodes.what: The Web cluck captions drawn as text over the canvas, following their chicken.

nodes.label: Web follow-source fix
nodes.what: Captions follow their chicken as in Fizz 1, cut off by the frame's edge, instead of pinning to it.

nodes.label: Machine model
nodes.what: fizz-machine: the pure start-up check and settings model, with the probe data, the resolver, the OPL write router and the screen builder, tested on the host.

nodes.label: /CHECK screen and /CHECKCELLS (P-C)
